issues.description: Return-type and collection-type mismatch for retrieving all persons. The problem statement (and the client code) expect GET /persons to return a List<Person> (an ordered list). The template PersonService.getAllPersons method signature returns a List<Person>. However, the solution implementation of PersonService.getAllPersons returns a Set<Person> (and specifically a HashSet) while PersonResource.getAllPersons still declares ResponseEntity<List<Person>> and calls personService.getAllPersons(...). This creates two problems: (1) a method return-type mismatch between solution PersonService (Set<Person>) and the expected List<Person> used by PersonResource and the client (would cause compilation errors), and (2) returning a HashSet discards the ordering produced by the sorting logic, contradicting the intended sorting functionality described in the problem statement.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the service method return type consistent with the problem statement and client expectations: change PersonService.getAllPersons to return a List<Person> (preserving the sorted order). Concretely, update the signature to public List<Person> getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions) and return an ordered List (e.g. Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedList) or new ArrayList<>(sortedList)). Avoid returning a HashSet because it does not preserve sorting order and will contradict the sorting feature.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect/getAllPersons to work with a LIST of Person objects (the task text explicitly speaks of sorting "the list of Person" and the client expects a List<Person>). In the solution repository, PersonService.getAllPersons is changed to return a Set<Person> (and the implementation converts a sorted List into a HashSet), while PersonResource and the client still use List<Person>. This discrepancy (List vs Set) is a semantic inconsistency: the same conceptual entity (the collection of persons returned by getAllPersons, which must be ordered for sorting) is represented with different types across artifacts. It creates confusion about the expected return type and order-preservation (a Set does not guarantee order), and forces students to reconcile conflicting API expectations between service, controller/resource, and client.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the representation consistent: have PersonService.getAllPersons use and return a List<Person> (preserving sort order). Change the solution service signature to public List<Person> getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions) and return the sorted list (e.g. return Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedList) or new ArrayList<>(sortedList)). This keeps the service, controller/resource, client, and problem description aligned and preserves ordering semantics required for sorting.
